question: The expression for acceleration due to gravity on the surface of a planet of mass M and radius R is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**g = GM / R²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Acceleration due to gravity** is the force experienced by an object of unit mass due to the gravitational pull of a celestial body (planet, star, etc.). It is denoted by **g**.
 
• The formula for calculating acceleration due to gravity on the surface of a planet is derived from **Newton's Law of Gravitation**.
 
• The gravitational force is given by the formula: **F = GMm / R²**, where:
 
 
• **G**: Universal gravitational constant (6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg²).
 
• **M**: Mass of the planet.
 
• **m**: Mass of the object experiencing the force.
 
• **R**: Radius of the planet.
 
 
 
• The acceleration due to gravity, **g**, is derived by dividing the gravitational force by the mass of the object:
 
 
• **g = F/m = GM/R²**.
